rationale: PINS the inherited type of a const spec, the Go const grammar's own macro. Go spec: 'Within a parenthesized const declaration list the empty expression list is equivalent to the textual substitution of the first preceding non-empty expression list and its type if present'. So in `const ( FormatUnknown Format = iota; formatV7; FormatUSTAR )` all three constants have type Format, and the latter two carry a real type reference the graph was MISSING. MEASURED DEFECT, proven before the fix on this exact fixture: only `references FormatUnknown -> Format` was published; `formatV7 -> Format` and `FormatUSTAR -> Format` were ABSENT. Not mis-sourced — absent, because `collectTypeNameNodes` collects only `type_identifier`/`qualified_type` and an inheriting spec has no type child at all, so `emit` had nothing to walk. REAL CORPUS FREQUENCY: measured over the Go corpus, 2,305 of 2,450 const groups (94%) use the implicit form, so this was the COMMON case rather than an edge case — `src/archive/tar/format.go` alone was missing `formatV7 -> Format @57`, `FormatUSTAR -> Format @68`, `FormatPAX -> Format @84`, `FormatGNU -> Format @98`, `formatSTAR -> Format @103` and `formatMax -> Format @105`. THE FIX IS SHAPE-PROVEN, NEVER NAME-BASED: the analyzer walks back to the nearest preceding sibling `const_spec` that HAS a `type` field and takes that node as the type root, leaving the emitter unchanged so the qualified-type and dedupe rules are identical for an inherited and a stated type. LINE NUMBERS ARE THE DECLARING SPEC'S OWN, and this is pinned: an inherited type node belongs to an EARLIER spec, so publishing the type node's line would point the row at a declaration it does not describe. Sibling lookup is a byte-span scan because `prevSibling` does not exist on this tree-sitter binding and wrapper objects are not identity-stable across `children` reads — the same technique real-protobuf-analyzer's `prevSiblingOf` established. THE FORBIDDEN ROWS ARE THE OTHER HALF, each a shape a cheaper fix would get wrong: (a) `B -> Other` is forbidden because group 1's `Format` must not leak into group 2 — a fix that scanned all previous specs in the FILE rather than the GROUP would claim it; (b) `D -> Format` is forbidden because group 2 has no type ANYWHERE (`D = 1` states an expression, not a type), so a fix that defaulted to a non-null type root would invent one; (c) `E -> Format` is forbidden for the same reason, and additionally pins that a typeless spec does not inherit through the group boundary; (d) `G -> Format` is forbidden in group 3 only for `G = 100`, which is a typeless EXPRESSION spec — it must not become a type SOURCE for `H` that follows it, and `H -> Format` is expected precisely because the walk skips the typeless list and keeps the real `F Format = iota`. NOT PINNED: confidence (every row is 0.95 structural, identical for any declared-type reference) and the symbol/exports rows, which the export pass owns unchanged.

expectRelationships.comment: A spec that STATES its type publishes the reference, as before the fix.
A spec with no type child INHERITS the previous spec's type: a real Format reference on its own declaration line.
The second inheritance in the same group, on its own line.
A second group proves the walk is not a one-shot: the first spec of group 2 states Other.
Inheritance in the second group, resolved against THAT group's base type.
Second inheritance in the second group.

forbidRelationships.comment: Group 1's Format must not leak into group 2. A fix that scanned all previous specs in the FILE instead of stopping at the group boundary would claim this.
Group 2's type is Other, so Format is wrong for every member of that group.
The LINE must be the declaring spec's own. An inherited type node belongs to an earlier spec, so a fix that kept the type node's line would report 15 instead of 16.
Same line defect on the second inheriting spec: it declares on 17, not on the 15 the borrowed type node carries.
